verses.text: These are the words of King Lemuel, the revelation his mother taught him:
“Oh, my son! The son I carried, the son of my vows!
Don't give your strength away to women or follow the ways that ruin kings.
Lemuel, kings have no business drinking wine. Rulers have no business asking where the strong drink is.
They might drink and forget the law, twisting the justice that people in trouble are owed.
Give strong drink to someone who's about to die, and wine to someone bitter in soul.
Let them drink and forget their poverty, and let their misery slip from their mind.
Speak up for those who can't speak, and take up the cause of everyone left helpless.
Speak up and judge fairly. Get justice for the poor and needy.”
Who can find a worthy woman? She's worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her with his whole heart, and he'll have no shortage of gain.
She does him good and never harms him, all the days of her life.
She looks for wool and flax and gets to work gladly with her hands.
She's like a fleet of merchant ships, bringing her food from far away.
She gets up while it's still dark, feeds her household, and sets out portions for the young women who serve her.
She sizes up a field and buys it. From what her own hands earn, she plants a vineyard.
She gets herself ready with strength and makes her arms strong.
She sees that her business is making a profit. Her lamp stays lit at night.
She reaches for the distaff and takes the spindle in her hands.
She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out to people in need.
She doesn't fear snow for her household. Everyone in the house is dressed in scarlet.
She makes her own coverings. She dresses in fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.
She makes linen clothes and sells them. She supplies sashes to the merchant.
She wears strength and dignity like clothes. She can laugh at what's ahead.
When she speaks, wisdom comes out. She teaches with kindness.
She watches over how her household is doing. She doesn't eat the bread of idleness.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too:
“Many women do noble things, but you rise above them all.”
Charm can fool you, and beauty doesn't last. A woman who reveres the LORD deserves praise.
Give her what her work has earned. Let what she's done bring her praise at the city gates!
